clue.text: See 14
See 14
Bowler for Yorkshire v Lancashire, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a bowler hat, called by this name in America
a match between local rivals, such as these two neighbouring English counties, is a local contest of this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests a cricketer, which fits the county match, but it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowler hats are called by this name in the US, and a game between near neighbours is a local grudge match of the same name.

clue.text: Elton, the criminal, extended appeal

indicators.note: criminal here means crooked or bent out of shape, signalling that Elton and the are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elton John, the convicted crook, launches a lengthy appeal against his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' is the anagram signal, with 'the' doing double duty in the surface but serving as fodder: ELTON plus THE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A long televised fundraising broadcast is an appeal for charity stretched over many hours.

clue.text: See 14
Pacific islands in this way break a criminal up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole string of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: so means in this way
a gap is a break or interval
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: Islanders in the Pacific help a crook escape by breaking him out.
explanation.walkthrough: SO GAP A LAG, read upwards as one run ('up'), gives the islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Galapagos are an archipelago in the Pacific Ocean belonging to Ecuador.

clue.text: Tea in tea's gone to pot

indicators.note: something gone to pot is ruined and jumbled, so the letters of in tea's are rearranged

parts.note: the word teas, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the tea they were served has been spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone to pot' jumbles IN TEAS. A pot is also where tea is made, a neat surface touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a kind of tea, usually made without tea leaves.

clue.text: Policeman is very suspicious of chartered organisations

indicators.note: suspicious suggests something fishy or off, telling the solver to rearrange the letters of policeman is very

explanation.surface: An officer harbours doubts about some officially sanctioned bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicious' rearranges all fifteen letters of POLICEMAN IS VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the ancient trade guilds of the City of London, each incorporated by royal charter.

clue.text: Two US leaders, Australian long jumper and Spanish golfer left gutted

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a long-jumping Australian animal
Seve Ballesteros, the Spanish golfer known by his first name

indicators.note: a gutted word loses its insides, so only the outer letters of left remain

explanation.surface: A gathering of two American presidents, an Australian athlete and a Spanish golfer who is left devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long jumper' sounds like an athlete but is a kangaroo. LEFT 'gutted' loses EF to leave LT.
explanation.definitionFit: Two US presidents, Theodore and Franklin D., shared this surname.

clue.text: Defence of California resort unbounded by Italy

indicators.note: without its bounds, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Malibu is a beach resort in California
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Californian beach town is defended, with Italy surrounding it.
explanation.walkthrough: MALIBU 'unbounded' loses its first and last letters to give ALIB; add I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence in law that the accused was somewhere else at the time.

clue.text: Famous chair only?

definitions.meaning: a chair alone is ..., read as three words: not a table

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as NOT A (T)ABLE run together: a chair on its own is not a table, so the question mark flags the loose wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable is famous or worthy of attention.

clue.text: Greek character with identity about to issue forth

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the combined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a name is one's identity

explanation.surface: A Greek person, along with an identity card, is about to come out.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA with NAME gives ETANAME; 'about' reverses the whole run. 'about to' looks like 'soon', but 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or proceed from a source, so it means to issue forth.

clue.text: I put on gravy, but not to bird

indicators.note: signals that the word to is taken out of the gravy brand

parts.note: Bisto is a well-known British brand of gravy granules
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner pours gravy over their food but not over the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Bisto is a gravy brand sold across Britain; 'put on' is only a link placing I first. 'bird' looks like the food being served but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: 17 across's negotiable version of Einstein's special theory of relativity: "Hokum! He PhD? Or me?"

definitions.note: the quip belongs to the comedian at 17 across, a famous line of his

indicators.note: something negotiable can be bargained into a different shape, so these clue letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mocking dismissal of Einstein's theory, sneering that neither a doctor nor the speaker could believe such nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all 48 letters of EINSTEINS SPECIAL THEORY OF RELATIVITY HOKUM HE PHD OR ME; the 's of Einstein's supplies its S. The quotation's point is that principles are negotiable, which the clue's 'negotiable' echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous wisecrack about flexible principles is attributed to the comedian Groucho Marx.

clue.text: On which bouncer with endless drug has to leave club

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
to go is to leave
a stick is a club or cudgel

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer with a drug habit is told to leave the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a doorman; here it is a person bouncing on the toy. POT 'endless' gives PO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pogo stick is a spring-loaded pole that a person stands on to bounce along.

clue.text: Rest of song now wrong

parts.note: a lied is a German art song

indicators.note: wrong means set out incorrectly, so now is rearranged

explanation.surface: The remainder of the song is now wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like a noun meaning remainder, as the surface reads it, but it is the verb; a lied is the German art song of Schubert and Schumann.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to rest, matching it as a verb.

clue.text: Curry unfinished, a lot eaten but no starter, leaving marks we hear

indicators.note: UCH is consumed by the other piece, sitting inside it
unfinished removes the final letter

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so having no starter means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: much means a lot

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a takeaway curry half-finished after eating a lot of it.
explanation.walkthrough: GROO (curry, unfinished) eats UCH (much, no starter). 'Marks we hear' sounds like Marx, the comedy brothers; 'leaving' is a link. 'Curry' is the verb meaning groom, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was one of the Marx Brothers, and Marx sounds like marks when spoken.

clue.text: Crybaby girl about to grab sleep? Elizabeth

indicators.note: the rearranged girl holds the sleep letters inside
about means moved around, so the letters of girl are rearranged

parts.note: zz is the comic-strip sign for sleep
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: A whining girl is about to grab some sleep, says Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'soon', but 'about' rearranges GIRL to GRIL, which grabs ZZ; then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A grizzler is someone who whimpers and complains, like a whining child.

clue.text: Red key

definitions.meaning: a deep scarlet colour, as worn by senior Catholic clergy

explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal red is a vivid scarlet, and a cardinal point or rule is a key, central one.

clue.text: Popeye with claim on Donald Duck?

parts.note: Popeye is a cartoon sailor
a suit is a legal claim

explanation.surface: Popeye files a lawsuit against Donald Duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what Donald Duck wears: the cartoon duck is drawn in a sailor's blouse and cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Duck's familiar outfit is a navy blouse with a cap, the costume of a seaman.

clue.text: I … I … imbeciles

parts.note: the letter I with trailing dots, then another I among dots: read as I with dots, I inside

explanation.surface: A speaker stammers in exasperation at some fools.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is read as I followed by DOTS with a second I set among the dots, giving I, D(I)OTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots and imbeciles are both insulting words for stupid people.

clue.text: Elf wound round end of finger

indicators.note: spite goes round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to spite someone is to hurt or wound them

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of finger

explanation.surface: A bandage is wound round the tip of a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as a bandage being wrapped, but it is the verb to hurt, SPITE, which goes 'round' R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a fairy or elf in folklore.

clue.text: Seeping bit of liquid, having weed

explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a falling drop of liquid, and also slang for a weak, wet person.

clue.text: Soundly smooth flat land

indicators.note: soundly here means as heard, signalling a word with the same sound

parts.note: to plane wood is to smooth it

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps soundly on a smooth, level field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like an adverb of thoroughness but signals the homophone of PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is a large expanse of flat, open land.

clue.text: Waste which takes a battering?

definitions.meaning: to squander time or money, used as a verb
a piece of food coated in batter and fried

explanation.definitionFit: To fritter away is to waste, and a fritter is a battered, fried snack.

clue.text: Huge figure, brave character to follow nation lacking support

indicators.note: the brave animal comes after the shortened nation
the support letters are taken away from the nation

parts.note: Brazil is a country
a bra is a support garment
the lion is proverbially brave

explanation.surface: A brave figure follows a nation that is short of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' as an undergarment is the trick; 'to follow' places the brave animal after the shortened country.
explanation.definitionFit: A zillion is an informal word for an enormous, unspecified number.

clue.text: Sort of nerve through which spirit?

definitions.meaning: the nerve that carries signals from the eye to the brain
the measuring device fixed to an upturned bottle in a British pub, dispensing a measure of spirits

explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs, spirits are poured through an inverted-bottle measure with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic nerve serves the eye, and an Optic is a bar device dispensing measures of spirits.
